intent: Explore without an advancement verdict whether one screened vacuum-response field can recover Newtonian gravity in dense regions, build up in extended low-density regions, and generate useful galaxy, cluster, geometry, and diagnostic-lensing behavior.

equations.outer_boundary: Sigma approaches 1 in an extended vacuum

spherical_galaxy.comparison_only: fixed empirical RAR with g_dagger=1.2e-10 m/s^2

cluster_transfer.warning: The target is NFW-deprojected and is used only to rank this exploratory grid.

void_buildup.geometry: empty spherical cavity with Sigma=0 at a dense wall

lensing.closure: same effective potential, zero gravitational slip, no lensing multiplier
lensing.fit: six common structural geometry/shear nuisances on 15 training images; exact roots on seven spent heldout images
lensing.warning: Diagnostic only because the ranked parameters use the RXJ2129 NFW-deprojected radial target and the image holdout has already been inspected.

interpretation_rules: This is a permissive exploration, not a preregistered theory acceptance test.
Do not insert RAR, MOND, a cluster label, coherence, or a lensing normalization into the Sigma-field prediction.
Separate mathematical behavior from empirical closeness.
A zero-slip lensing calculation is not a relativistic completion.
Report parameter tradeoffs and structural limitations even if one score is promising.
